candidates.attacker_control: An unauthenticated network client that can reach the ONOS HTTP port (Pax-Web default 8181, tools/package/etc/org.ops4j.pax.web.cfg) fully controls the HTTP method, path and JSON body of requests; no credentials, session or token are required for the affected WAB contexts (e.g. /onos/restconf/*, /onos/vtn/*, /onos/virtualbng/*, /onos/mfwd/*, /onos/kafka/*, /onos/openstacknetworkingui/*, /onos/v1/fm/*).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The omission is not a global policy: web/api (lines 25-42), acl, castor, cfm, dhcp, segmentrouting, mcast, route-service and many other WABs do declare the admin BASIC security-constraint, so unconstrained WABs deviate from the project pattern. The core /onos/v1 REST API and GUI index are protected. Affected apps are optional add-ons, not the minimal default app set, and I could not run Pax-Web to confirm runtime de-duplication/merge of constraints; the claim rests on standard WAB/security-constraint semantics. Environment hardening (authenticating proxy, firewall on 8181, unused optional apps) would mitigate. Some instances (apps/yang/web) are not built in this snapshot, so I did not rely on them.
candidates.impact: Remote, unauthenticated read and modification of controller/network state: RESTCONF exposes the ONOS dynamic configuration store (device/network configuration) for GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE plus RPC invocation and notification subscriptions; VTN exposes create/update/delete of tenant networks, subnets, routers, virtual ports, floating IPs and port chains, which map to intents/flow rules; VBNG exposes address-mapping manipulation; fault-management, mfwd and Kafka-integration endpoints are likewise unauthenticated. This can produce network-wide misconfiguration/denial of service and disclosure of topology/configuration data. No arbitrary-code-execution primitive was confirmed from this root cause, though control-plane compromise is significant.
candidates.prerequisites: The corresponding optional ONOS app/WAB must be installed and activated (e.g. org.onosproject.protocols.restconfserver, org.onosproject.vtn, org.onosproject.virtualbng, org.onosproject.mfwd, org.onosproject.kafkaintegration, org.onosproject.openstacknetworkingui, org.onosproject.faultmanagement); attacker must have TCP access to 8181; no authenticating reverse proxy or network ACL in front of ONOS; per-WAB security constraints are the only auth mechanism. The apps/yang/web bundle is present as sources but has no pom.xml in this snapshot and is not built.
candidates.root_cause: Multiple ONOS web-application bundles (WABs) declare a JAX-RS ServletContainer mapped to /* but their WEB-INF/web.xml contains no active <security-constraint>/<auth-constraint> (role admin, BASIC realm karaf), unlike sibling WABs such as web/api, acl, dhcp and segmentrouting. Under Pax-Web/Karaf the per-WAB web.xml is the only authentication mechanism, so JAX-RS resources of an unconstrained WAB are served without any JAAS login. In apps/vtn/vtnweb/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml the constraint block exists but is commented out (lines 23-42) with the literal comment 'TODO: this should be uncommented', and in protocols/restconf/server/rpp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml the constraint is absent altogether.
candidates.title: ONOS application REST endpoints (RESTCONF server, VTN web, and other WABs) are deployed without authentication
candidates.trace: Unauthenticated HTTP request -> Pax-Web/Jetty routes to the bundle's Jersey ServletContainer because the WAB descriptor has no <security-constraint>, so no JAAS check occurs -> RESTCONF example: PUT/POST/DELETE/PATCH /onos/restconf/data/{identifier} reaches RestconfWebResource.handlePutRequest/handlePostRequest/handleDeleteRequest (lines 192-300+) -> RestconfManager.runPostOperationOnDataResource/runPutOperationOnDataResource/runDeleteOperationOnDataResource (lines 136-216) -> DynamicConfigService.createNode/replaceNode/deleteNode, i.e. persistent controller configuration that is pushed to managed devices; GET /onos/restconf/data/... returns stored configuration, and /onos/restconf/streams/{id} registers an event stream. VTN example: POST /onos/vtn/networks -> TenantNetworkWebResource (@Path("networks"), line 66) -> TenantNetworkService/intent layer. VBNG example: POST/DELETE /onos/virtualbng/privateip/... -> VbngResource lines 42-96.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: no ONOS instance was started and no HTTP requests were sent. The exact set of apps activated in the graded deployment is unknown, and I could not verify whether Karaf/Pax-Web 3.x applies any implicit authentication for WABs without constraints (source and sibling descriptors indicate it does not). Whether the benchmark's expected issue is one specific instance (e.g. VTN vs RESTCONF) rather than the systemic omission is also unverified, which is why multiple same-root-cause descriptors are listed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function (also CWE-862)

coverage_summary: Scope tool reported 8032 model-visible text files (no sensitive-name/path or size exclusions; binaries skipped). The snapshot has no test sources at all (all src/test content absent), so review is main-source only. I read/inspected: root and app poms (version 1.14.0-SNAPSHOT), all 31 web.xml/WAB descriptors, web/api REST resources and web.xml, the whole NetworkConfig/ComponentConfig/Applications/DeviceKey web resources, protocols/restconf server + apps/restconf service chain, apps/vtn/vtnweb resources, apps/yang live compiler and web module, drivers/netconf TemplateManager and drivers/utilities XmlConfigParser, providers/netconf alarm translator, core/common ApplicationArchive, incubator gRPC servers, packaging/etc configuration, and several app web resources (castor, virtualbng, mfwd, kafka, dhcp, cpman). Large unexamined areas remain: protocol/packet parsers, drivers per-vendor code, GUI JavaScript/assets, models, and much of core/store and providers. Line numbers are from the read-only text tools.
limitations: No code was executed, built, or fuzzed; all conclusions are static and no HTTP/runtime behavior was verified, so the candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

The candidate relies on standard J2EE/Pax-Web semantics: a WAB without an active security-constraint serves its context unauthenticated. I could not run Karaf/Pax-Web to confirm there is no implicit global authentication, though sibling WAB descriptors and the project's own TODOs indicate there is none.
Affected apps are optional add-ons; whether they are installed/activated in the graded environment is unknown and affects reachability.
No CVE/patch/ground-truth data could be consulted (forbidden), so the mapping of this root cause to any particular advisory is unverified.
This review sampled the repository; many parsers/protocols/drivers and all tests were not inspected, so other vulnerabilities may exist that I did not evaluate.
Because only one candidate may be submitted, the zip-slip, XXE, trust-all TLS, gRPC and default-credential leads above were not submitted even though several are plausibly real.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip / path traversal in apps/yang/src/main/java/org/onosproject/yang/impl/YangLiveCompilerManager.java (extractZipArchive, lines 117-131): zip entry names are passed to new File(dir, entry.getName()) and Files.write without canonical-path validation.
rejected_leads.reason: Real unvalidated path construction, but in this snapshot the HTTP trigger (apps/yang/web upload) is not built (no pom.xml and no module reference), so in-tree reachability is only the local CLI path; also no remote attacker control over the zip without admin credentials. Keep as a secondary lead only.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip / path traversal in core/common/src/main/java/org/onosproject/common/app/ApplicationArchive.java (expandZippedApplication, lines 349-372): isTopLevel() checks only file.getName(), so entries like '../../x.jar' still pass and are written outside appsDir.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires application-install privilege (admin REST/CLI), which is already a highly privileged operation (installing an ONOS app bundle already executes attacker-supplied code), so the security gain is limited.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in unhardened XML parsers: drivers/netconf/src/main/java/org/onosproject/drivers/netconf/TemplateManager.java (lines 60-66), protocols/xmpp/core/ctl/src/main/java/org/onosproject/xmpp/core/ctl/handlers/XmlMerger.java (lines 57-62), utils/misc/src/main/java/org/onlab/util/XmlString.java (lines 71-78), apps/odtn/api/src/main/java/org/onosproject/odtn/utils/YangToolUtil.java (lines 196-217). Notably XmlConfigParser and NetconfAlarmTranslator in the same tree already contain DTD-disabling hardening, showing the omission pattern.
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker-controlled XML must come from a malicious/compromised NETCONF device or XMPP server (or local CLI for ODTN), i.e. device/peer compromise rather than direct remote network access, so lower than the unauthenticated-API candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Trust-all TLS X509TrustManager implementations in protocols/rest/api/.../HttpSBControllerImpl.java (lines ~330-345), providers/rest/device/.../RestDeviceProviderUtilities.java (lines ~60-70), apps/openstacknetworking/.../OpenstackNetworkingUtil.java (lines ~380-405) and apps/openstacknode/.../OpenstackNodeUtil.java (lines ~170-190).
rejected_leads.reason: Enables MITM of southbound/Keystone HTTPS connections, but exploitation requires on-path position and the credentials impact is indirect; not the strongest single finding.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated gRPC northbound servers: incubator/protobuf/registry/.../GrpcServiceRegistryImpl.java (creates ServerBuilder.forPort without TLS/auth, lines 184-205), incubator/rpc-nb/.../GrpcServer.java (port 50051 plaintext, lines 61-71), and incubator/protobuf/services/nb/.../GrpcNbComponentConfigService.java Class.forName on a client-supplied class name (lines 110-130).
rejected_leads.reason: Same CWE-306 class but confined to optional incubator apps that must be installed, and I could not confirm default activation; the web WAB instances are more clearly deployed by the standard app set.

rejected_leads.lead: Default credentials shipped in tools/package/etc/users.properties (karaf/karaf, onos/rocks, guest/guest, lines 32-36).
rejected_leads.reason: Well-known documented ONOS defaults and changeable by the operator; a configuration weakness rather than a code vulnerability, and the missing-auth WABs need no credentials at all.

rejected_leads.lead: Command construction in apps/cip/src/main/java/org/onosproject/cip/ClusterIpManager.java (lines 155-167) concatenates component-config values into Runtime.exec(String).
rejected_leads.reason: Runtime.exec(String) does not invoke a shell, so only argument injection into 'sudo ifconfig' is possible, and the values are set by an authenticated administrator via component config; weak exploitability.

rejected_leads.lead: 'Post-processed raw' GUI resource web/gui/.../FooResource.java and extension resource serving (MainViewResource) use path parameters, and MainIndexResource injects the user name into JavaScript (lines 97-103).
rejected_leads.reason: ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream limits reads to classpath resources and the JS injection is effectively self-XSS for the authenticated user; no cross-user impact established.

summary: ONOS 1.14.0-SNAPSHOT (mid-2018 master) review. I surveyed the build/version metadata, the web/api REST resources, all WAB descriptors (web.xml), RESTCONF/VTN/YANG/ODTN/OpenStack app modules, NETCONF/XML parsing code, core application-archive handling, incubator gRPC servers, and packaging config. Strongest source-evidenced issue: several ONOS web-application bundles deploy a JAX-RS servlet mapped to /* with no active security-constraint, so their REST endpoints are reachable without authentication; the VTN descriptor even carries the intended constraint commented out with a TODO, and the RESTCONF proxy descriptor omits it entirely. This yields unauthenticated read/modify of controller configuration/state (RESTCONF dynamic config, VTN virtual networks, VBNG mappings, etc.). Other plausible but weaker leads (zip-slip in zip extractors, unhardened XXE parsers, trust-all TLS managers, unauthenticated incubator gRPC, default credentials) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads.
